trials.name: A4
trials.population: Older individuals with preclinical Alzheimer's disease (elevated brain amyloid but cognitively normal)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline of the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC) Score
trials.results_summary: Solanezumab did not slow cognitive decline or reduce the risk of progression to symptomatic Alzheimer's disease compared to placebo.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2
trials.population: Participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS)
trials.results_summary: Donanemab significantly slowed clinical decline at 76 weeks compared to placebo. This trial successfully utilized p-tau217 blood biomarkers for patient screening and stratification.

trials.name: BioFINDER - Primary Care
trials.population: Primary care patients evaluated for cognitive impairment
trials.primary_endpoint: Presence of brain AD pathology as determined by CSF AD biomarkers
trials.results_summary: Interim results published in JAMA (2024) demonstrated that plasma p-tau217, combined with a brief memory test, accurately diagnoses AD in primary care settings (approx 90% accuracy).

trials.name: AHEAD 3-45
trials.population: Participants with preclinical Alzheimer's disease (elevated or intermediate amyloid)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5) Score at Week 216

related_evidence.description: NEJM publication of the A4 trial results showing solanezumab failed to slow cognitive decline in preclinical AD.
JAMA publication of TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 showing donanemab's efficacy, highlighting the successful use of p-tau217 for trial stratification.
JAMA publication by first author O. Hansson confirming plasma p-tau217's high diagnostic accuracy in diverse primary care cohorts (BioFINDER PC).

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence strongly supports the document's central claims regarding the high diagnostic accuracy of plasma p-tau217 and its utility in trial prescreening. While the document's authors have severe conflicts of interest—including patent holdings for p-tau217 (J.D.) and ownership of Brain Biomarker Solutions—subsequent landmark phase 3 trials (e.g., TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2) independently validated p-tau217's utility for efficiently stratifying and screening AD patients. Furthermore, the review's noted limitation regarding a lack of prospective, real-world primary care validation has been actively addressed by the authors' ongoing BioFINDER-Primary Care study (NCT06120361), which demonstrated over 90% diagnostic accuracy for p-tau217 in a 2024 interim readout. The document's critique of historical trial inefficiencies is fully corroborated by the failure of the A4 trial (NCT02008357), which required massive, costly PET screening efforts; ongoing preclinical trials like AHEAD 3-45 are now successfully leveraging blood biomarkers to reduce these bottlenecks.
